title: Star Trek · Starships Through Time
scope: Selected individual spacecraft, not complete fleet inventories or class production runs.
date_policy: Earth calendar chronology, interpreted from screen dates, stardates and relative dialogue. Unknown construction/launch dates are null. Selected attested years are not exhaustive service endpoints.

ships.name: Phoenix
ships.note: Cochrane's first human warp flight: 5 April. A converted missile, built in Montana.

ships.name: T'Plana-Hath
ships.note: Detects Phoenix's warp signature; its landing initiates public human–Vulcan contact.

ships.name: Friendship 1
ships.note: Launched to share human knowledge. Voyager recovers its wreckage in 2378.

ships.name: SS Conestoga
ships.note: Nine-year voyage to Terra Nova; dismantled into buildings on arrival in 2078.

ships.name: ECS Horizon
ships.note: Travis Mayweather's family cargo ship. His birth aboard in 2126 anchors its earlier use.
ships.qualifier: Commissioning in 2102 follows the ship and class histories; 2126 and 2153 are selected later attested years.

ships.name: Kumari
ships.note: Shran's command from 2142. A Romulan drone destroys the ship in 2154.

ships.name: NX-Alpha
ships.note: A. G. Robinson exceeds warp 2; loss of the prototype exposes engine instability.

ships.name: NX-Beta
ships.note: Archer and Robinson reach warp 2.5 on an unauthorized test and return safely.

ships.name: NX-Delta
ships.note: Duvall's warp 3 trial continues the engine program that leads to the NX-class.
ships.qualifier: Relative dating is approximately 2144–2145: reference pages differ by one year. The craft is mentioned, not depicted.

ships.name: Enterprise NX-01
ships.note: Archer's warp 5 explorer fights the Xindi crisis; retired in 2161, later preserved.
ships.credit: ENT · Broken Bow; These Are the Voyages…

ships.name: ECS Fortunate
ships.note: A family-operated cargo ship targeted by Nausicaan raiders. Construction year unstated.

ships.name: Vahklas
ships.note: Transports the V'tosh ka'tur. Enterprise assists with repairs during its journey.

ships.name: D'kyr
ships.note: Rendezvous ship for Enterprise's canceled mission; its crew monitors the Suliban confrontation.

ships.name: Columbia NX-02
ships.note: Under construction in 2153. Engine trouble delays launch; Hernandez takes command.

ships.name: USS Enterprise
ships.note: April, Pike and Kirk's ship; extensively refit in the 2270s. Scuttled above Genesis in 2285.

ships.name: USS Shenzhou
ships.note: Georgiou's veteran vessel. Abandoned after the Battle at the Binary Stars in 2256.
ships.credit: DIS · The Vulcan Hello; Battle at the Binary Stars
ships.qualifier: In service by 2249; construction and launch years are not established here.

ships.name: USS Discovery
ships.note: Spore-drive research ship. Leaves 2258 for 3189; the gap is time travel, not service.
ships.credit: DIS · Context Is for Kings; Such Sweet Sorrow II
ships.qualifier: Active again in 3189–3191 and in the 33rd-century coda; the exact coda year is not used.

ships.name: USS Glenn
ships.note: Sister ship in the spore-drive program. A failed jump kills the crew; Discovery scuttles it.

ships.name: USS Farragut
ships.note: Kirk's early posting. The 2257 cloud-creature attack kills crew, not the ship itself.
ships.credit: TOS · Obsession; SNW · Lost in Translation
ships.qualifier: The 2243 launch plaque is shown in an alternate-future episode; it is not adopted as a Prime launch date here.

ships.name: USS Archer
ships.note: A three-person first-contact mission to Kiley 279 requires Enterprise's intervention.
ships.qualifier: Often catalogued as Gral-class; a screen-neutral scout descriptor avoids implying a spoken class name.

ships.name: Romulan Bird-of-Prey
ships.note: Cloaked ship attacks Federation outposts; its commander destroys it after defeat.

ships.name: USS Constellation
ships.note: Decker's disabled cruiser is sent inside the planet killer, destroying both vessels.
ships.credit: PIC · The Star Gazer plaque; SNW · Terrarium; TOS · The Doomsday Machine
ships.qualifier: The 2245 launch is recorded on the screen commemorative plaque. Later years are selected mission attestations.

ships.name: IKS Gr'oth
ships.note: Confronts Enterprise at Deep Space K-7 during the tribble incident.
ships.credit: TOS · The Trouble with Tribbles; DS9 · Trials…

ships.name: USS Intrepid
ships.note: Crewed by Vulcans. Destroyed by the giant space organism in 2268.
ships.credit: TOS · Court Martial; The Immunity Syndrome

ships.name: USS Defiant
ships.note: Vanishes into spatial interphase; emerges in the Mirror Universe in 2155.
ships.credit: TOS · The Tholian Web; ENT · In a Mirror, Darkly

ships.name: USS Bozeman
ships.note: Time displacement carries Bateson's ship to 2368; it later fights at Sector 001 in 2373.
ships.credit: TNG · Cause and Effect; First Contact

ships.name: USS Reliant
ships.note: Genesis survey ship seized by Khan. Destroyed in the Mutara Nebula confrontation.

ships.name: USS Grissom
ships.note: Science vessel studying Genesis. Destroyed by Kruge's Bird-of-Prey.

ships.name: USS Excelsior
ships.note: Transwarp prototype becomes Sulu's command. Preserved at the Fleet Museum by 2401.
ships.credit: Films III, IV, VI; PIC · The Bounty
ships.qualifier: Launch in 2285 follows the dedication plaque; construction start and final retirement are not established here. Later dots are selected sightings.

ships.name: Kruge's ship / HMS Bounty
ships.note: Captured in 2285; transports whales from 1986 in 2286. Later recovered for the museum.

ships.name: USS Enterprise-A
ships.note: Commissioned for Kirk's crew. The Khitomer mission precedes retirement in 2293.
ships.credit: The Voyage Home; The Undiscovered Country

ships.name: Kronos One
ships.note: Carries Gorkon to peace talks; the attack on the ship triggers the Khitomer conspiracy.

ships.name: USS Enterprise-B
ships.note: Harriman's maiden voyage rescues El-Aurian refugees from the Nexus. Final fate unstated.

ships.name: USS Stargazer
ships.note: Picard commands from 2333; abandoned at Maxia in 2355, recovered in 2364, later a museum ship.
ships.credit: TNG · The Battle; PIC · The Bounty

ships.name: USS Enterprise-C
ships.note: Garrett's ship returns from an altered 2366 to defend Narendra III; destroyed in 2344.

ships.name: USS Enterprise-D
ships.note: Lost at Veridian III in 2371. Saucer rebuilt with Syracuse parts; back in action in 2401.
ships.credit: TNG; Generations; PIC · Võx; The Last Generation
ships.qualifier: 2363 follows the dedication plaque and commissioning chronology. The conflicting 2362 promotional-log date is not used. Restoration is not active service.

ships.name: USS Phoenix
ships.note: Built by Yoyodyne at 40 Eridani A; Maxwell's unauthorized Cardassian attacks occur in 2367.

ships.name: USS Yamato
ships.note: Iconian software disables safeguards and destroys the ship. Other hull graphics use different registries.

ships.name: USS Saratoga
ships.note: Destroyed at Wolf 359. Benjamin and Jake Sisko escape; Jennifer Sisko dies aboard.

ships.name: USS Rio Grande
ships.note: Sisko and Dax discover the Bajoran wormhole aboard this DS9 support craft in 2369.

ships.name: USS Odyssey
ships.note: A Jem'Hadar suicide attack destroys the ship during a Gamma Quadrant rescue mission.

ships.name: USS Defiant · prototype
ships.note: Launched in 2370; assigned to DS9 in 2371. Destroyed at the second Battle of Chin'toka.
ships.credit: DS9 · The Search; The Changing Face of Evil
ships.qualifier: Trials and storage precede DS9 service. Development began in 2366; this is not a 2366 launch.

ships.name: USS Equinox
ships.note: Science ship pulled into the Delta Quadrant. Destroyed after exploiting nucleogenic lifeforms.

ships.name: USS Voyager
ships.note: Seven-year Delta Quadrant journey ends in 2378. Preserved by 2381; no 2404 Prime return.

ships.name: USS Enterprise-E
ships.note: Fights the Borg and Shinzon. Its later loss of availability is mentioned; exact fate is unstated.
ships.qualifier: Selected screen-attested active years only. No 2385/2386 retirement or destruction date is inferred from promotional logs.

ships.name: USS Valiant
ships.note: A cadet training cruise becomes a wartime command; a Dominion battleship destroys it.

ships.name: USS Prometheus
ships.note: Experimental vessel with multi-vector assault mode; recovered from Romulan hijackers.
ships.credit: VOY · Message in a Bottle; Endgame

ships.name: Delta Flyer · first hull
ships.note: Paris's custom craft is built in the Delta Quadrant. Destroyed during the Borg infiltration.

ships.name: USS Sao Paulo → Defiant
ships.note: New hull replaces the lost Defiant in 2375. Still active in 2384; museum ship by 2401.
ships.credit: DS9 · The Dogs of War; PRO · Supernova I; PIC

ships.name: Delta Flyer · second hull
ships.note: Replacement built after the first Flyer's loss; Paris and Torres race it in Drive.

ships.name: USS Titan
ships.note: Riker's command after Nemesis. Helps Cerritos against the Pakleds; a different hull from Titan-A.
ships.credit: Nemesis; LD · No Small Parts; The New Next Generation
ships.qualifier: 2379 is Riker's command appointment, not a documented launch. Conflicting promotional retirement dates are excluded.

ships.name: USS Cerritos
ships.note: Second-contact workhorse under Freeman, then Ransom. Active through the Lower Decks finale.
ships.credit: LD · Second Contact; The New Next Generation
ships.qualifier: The 2371 launch given in a licensed crew handbook is not a screen-canon launch anchor.

ships.name: USS Solvang
ships.note: A brand-new California-class vessel; destroyed with all hands by a Pakled clumpship.

ships.name: USS Aledo
ships.note: Autonomous prototype attacks its creator; the California-class fleet destroys it.

ships.name: USS Protostar
ships.note: Launched for Chakotay; recovered by Dal's crew. Self-destructs in 2384 to stop the living construct.
ships.qualifier: Time travel also places this same hull before launch and after its destruction, including the repaired 2384–2385 loop. Those visits are not a continuous production/service interval.

ships.name: USS Dauntless
ships.note: Janeway's quantum-slipstream ship searches for Protostar. Distinct from Arturis's false Starfleet vessel.
ships.credit: PRO · A Moral Star II; Supernova I–II

ships.name: USS Voyager-A
ships.note: New Voyager launched six years after the original returns. Janeway's command passes to Chakotay.
ships.credit: PRO · Into the Breach; Ouroboros II

ships.name: USS Prodigy
ships.note: A new production-class ship for the young crew's exploration mission after the prototype's loss.

ships.name: USS Titan-A → Enterprise-G
ships.note: Shaw commands from 2396. Renamed Enterprise-G in 2402, with Seven of Nine in command.
ships.credit: PIC · The Next Generation; The Last Generation
ships.qualifier: 2396 is anchored by Shaw's five years in command, not a directly stated construction date. The 2402 change is a rename of the same hull.

ships.name: USS Stargazer
ships.note: Rios's four-nacelle command investigates the anomaly and encounters Jurati's Borg faction.

ships.name: USS Enterprise-F
ships.note: Shelby's Frontier Day flagship. Scheduled for early decommissioning; shown in action in 2401.
ships.qualifier: 2386 launch comes from promotional Picard Logs, not the screened story; no 2386–2401 bar is asserted.

ships.name: Krayton
ships.note: Tog's ship abducts Lwaxana and Deanna Troi and Commander Riker at Betazed.

ships.name: IKS Bortas
ships.note: Gowron's command during the succession crisis. Not the 22nd-century D5 with the same name.
ships.credit: TNG · The Defector; Redemption; Rightful Heir

ships.name: Trager
ships.note: Macet's cruiser participates in the pursuit of Maxwell's rogue USS Phoenix.

ships.name: Borg cube · Wolf 359
ships.note: Abducts Picard and destroys 39 ships at Wolf 359; destroyed near Earth in 2367.
ships.credit: TNG · The Best of Both Worlds I–II

ships.name: IRW Khazara
ships.note: Warbird used to smuggle Romulan dissidents while Troi impersonates a Tal Shiar officer.

ships.name: Koranak
ships.note: Part of the secret strike fleet; destroyed in the Dominion ambush at the Omarion Nebula.

ships.name: IKS Negh'Var
ships.note: Introduced as the new flagship for the invasion of Cardassia; later attacks Deep Space 9.
ships.credit: DS9 · The Way of the Warrior; By Inferno's Light

ships.name: IKS Rotarran
ships.note: Martok restores its demoralized crew in 2373 and retains it as his wartime flagship.
ships.credit: DS9 · Soldiers of the Empire; Inter Arma…

ships.name: Captured Jem'Hadar ship
ships.note: Salvaged by Starfleet in 2373; used against a ketracel-white depot, then crashes in 2374.
ships.credit: DS9 · The Ship; A Time to Stand; Rocks and Shoals

ships.name: Borg cube · Sector 001
ships.note: Destroyed by the fleet at Earth. Its escaping sphere travels back to 2063.

ships.name: Valdore
ships.note: Supports Enterprise-E against Scimitar in the Bassen Rift; damaged but survives.

ships.name: Scimitar
ships.note: Built in secret at Remus. Its thalaron weapon is destroyed by Data, taking the ship with it.

ships.name: The Artifact
ships.note: A reclamation site rather than an active Collective warship; flies to Coppelius and crashes.
ships.credit: PIC · The Impossible Box; Et in Arcadia Ego
ships.qualifier: 2399 covers Romulan reclamation and brief reactivation. Its manufacture and disconnection years are not specified here.

ships.name: USS Voyager-J
ships.note: A later bearer of Voyager's name with detached nacelles; distinct from Janeway's hull.
ships.credit: DIS · Die Trying; season 4; Red Directive
ships.qualifier: Selected dated observations; later appearances do not imply a 3191 retirement.

ships.name: USS Nog
ships.note: Part of the fleet around concealed Federation Headquarters when Discovery arrives.

ships.name: USS Tikhov
ships.note: Preserves the Federation's seed collection. A Barzan family tends the archive.

ships.name: USS Credence
ships.note: Distributes dilithium as the Federation reconnects worlds after the Burn.

ships.name: USS Athena
ships.note: Spaceborne home of the reopened Starfleet Academy; serves as both campus and starship.
ships.qualifier: Academy calendar dating is disputed (3192 versus 3195–3196 in indexed references). The poster shows the 3190s as an uncertain range, not an exact launch or service interval.
